description:
## Why this ticket exists

v0.2 (T-011) ships the *mechanism*: durable `service install|start|stop`, the launcher with an allowlisted 0600 path registry + persistent installation ID, and the control socket — all built on the T-008-adopted singleton primitive (kernel-held loopback port bind + write-once `link()` allocation; no lockfiles, no PID records, nothing reclaimed on the strength of an earlier observation). The plan is explicit that "v0.3 adds the full upgrade matrix, not the mechanism itself" — plus the menubar attach semantics that make the service/view split real. This ticket is also the carrier of the round-2 redesign's honesty stance: **no "automatic upgrade survival" claim**; the healing model is stated explicitly, and the degraded states this ticket produces are recorded so doctor (T-017) can explain them.

## Scope (in)

- **`spendbar menubar` = a view**: ensures the service is running (via the launcher), spawns the Swift helper (T-014), renders the snapshot. **Quit menubar ≠ Stop service** — both are explicit, separate actions.
- **Stop-service sequencing (ordering is load-bearing; final step corrected per ISS-041)**: (1) persist desired state as stopped → (2) **disable relaunch** (KeepAlive would otherwise respawn) → (3) request graceful shutdown **over the control socket** — the service, as the socket's owner, unlinks its own socket path and closes its listener (releasing the singleton port) on the way out; owner self-cleanup is not a reclaim and carries no race → (4) wait to deadline → (5) **then** boot out the launchd job → (6) verify termination, leaving any leftover socket file in place. Unloading first would kill the process before it receives the request. The former final step — "remove only a verified-stale socket" — is **deleted**: probe-then-unlink is a TOCTOU (ISS-041) in which another process can bind the pathname between the probe and the unlink, so the stop command could delete a LIVE server's socket; holding the singleton lock only narrows that window (it serializes cooperating spendbar instances, not arbitrary same-UID processes). Reclaiming a crash-leftover socket belongs exclusively to the next **service start**, which follows T-011's fixed startup order — validate write-once token → validate write-once allocation → acquire singleton port → probe the unix socket → reclaim only confirmed-stale → bind socket → serve — so reclaim happens while the port is held, and the residual same-UID interference from non-cooperating processes is accepted and documented, never claimed away. Each transition is failure-injected; `service start` reverses each partial-stop failure via that same startup order. **No PID-based control** (PID reuse); service identity is established by the port singleton's domain-separated HMAC challenge (ours / foreign / indeterminate — foreign and indeterminate both refuse), never by PID records or lockfiles.
- **LaunchAgent topology**: plists target the **launcher**, never `env node` (launchd PATH lacks package-manager paths); only the menubar view's agent carries `LimitLoadToSessionType: Aqua`; the service agent does not.
- **Headless defined honestly**: headless = no-menubar operation *within a logged-in user session*. LaunchAgents load at user login, so an SSH-only Mac with no GUI login gets **no reboot-persistence promise** — the documented path there is foreground `spendbar service run` (e.g. under tmux).
- **Full upgrade matrix**: reboot persistence on **Homebrew-node AND nvm machines**; npm upgrade; downgrade; prefix change; nvm version removal; interrupted install — each verified against **REAL Claude Code and REAL Codex MCP launches** (round-2 finding: shebang bins break under GUI-launched clients without the package manager's PATH; MCP registration goes through the launcher with an explicit `mcp` mode or validated absolute paths).
- **Ownership semantics exercised end-to-end**: a foreground command from a different prefix/version reports "another installation owns the service — run `spendbar service repair` to adopt" and never silently retargets; healing = the next foreground invocation of the *owning* installation re-validates + re-records, or explicit `repair`. Detection rides the launcher registry's installation ID plus the port challenge — never PID. Each ownership state is recorded with a machine-readable cause so doctor (T-017) can detect and explain it.

## Scope (out)

- Helper internals, title/menu rendering, crash-loop breaker (T-014).
- doctor/uninstall UX surfaces (T-017) — this ticket provides the **states and recorded diagnoses** they render; T-017 is deliberately not a blocker, so no acceptance criterion here may depend on doctor existing (ISS-026): this ticket's obligation ends at detectable states with recorded causes.
- The v0.2 mechanism itself (T-011) — extended and matrix-tested here, not rebuilt.
- Signing/notarization (T-016).

## Approach notes & constraints

- **The honest socket claim (ISS-041), stated once so no criterion overclaims**: the stop path never unlinks any socket pathname, so a live cooperating service's socket is never removed by stop; start-path reclaim removes only a socket whose holder failed the liveness probe while the singleton port is held; and the residual window — a non-cooperating same-UID process binding the pathname between probe and unlink — is accepted and documented, because closing it needs an atomic compare-and-act POSIX does not offer through Node (the same ceiling that eliminated the lockfile design in T-008). Any claim that the start-path window is narrow must be backed by an adversarial competing-binder test, not only cooperative failure injection.
- The "start menubar at login" consent in onboarding implies a second (Aqua-limited) LaunchAgent plist in v0.3, since SMAppService needs the flat `.app` (v0.5, or earlier only if D4 forces it).
- The matrix realistically needs clean VMs or clean user accounts with real reboots; the plan does not prescribe tooling — implementer's choice, but results must be recorded so a future session can re-check them.
- v0.3 phase exit applies: live $ ≤ 2 s; **survives service restarts AND package upgrades (post-heal)**.
- Carried unverified flag being retired here: "Launcher registry + LaunchAgent under real upgrade paths → v0.3 matrix".

## Acceptance criteria
1. On a machine with no running service, `spendbar menubar` starts the service through the launcher, spawns the helper, and shows live $ within ≤ 2 s warm.
2. After Quit-menubar, the service still answers a status request on the control socket (Quit menubar provably ≠ Stop service).
3. A stop-sequencing test asserts the exact 6-step order (persist state → disable relaunch → socket shutdown with owner self-cleanup → deadline wait → bootout → verify termination), with failure injection at every transition; KeepAlive does not respawn the stopped service; and the stop path performs NO unlink of the socket pathname — verified adversarially by a competing binder that takes the pathname mid-stop and observes its socket untouched (corrected per ISS-041: the former "no orphan socket remains" claim is dropped — after a forced bootout an orphan socket file may legitimately remain until the next start reclaims it, criterion 4).
4. After each injected partial-stop failure, `service start` recovers to a healthy running service via T-011's startup order (validate token → validate allocation → acquire port → probe socket → reclaim only confirmed-stale → bind → serve), reclaiming a leftover socket only after the singleton port is held and the probe confirms staleness; a bootout-killed service's orphan socket is reclaimed on exactly this path (reversal tested per transition).
5. Plist inspection tests: the service plist has no LimitLoadToSessionType, the menubar plist has Aqua, and both ProgramArguments target the launcher — never node directly or `env node`.
6. Matrix results are recorded (scripted runs + written outcomes) for: reboot on a Homebrew-node machine, reboot on an nvm machine, npm upgrade, downgrade, prefix change, nvm version removal, interrupted install — each ending in either a healthy service or an honestly-degraded state that is programmatically detectable with a recorded machine-readable cause (the input T-017's doctor will render; doctor's own explanation UX is verified in T-017, not here), and each verified with a real Claude Code launch AND a real Codex launch reaching the MCP server through the registered entry.
7. Foreign-installation test: with a second install at a different prefix, its foreground command prints the ownership-mismatch message and does not retarget (detection via installation ID + port challenge, never PID); `spendbar service repair` adopts; the owning installation's next foreground invocation re-validates + re-records after an upgrade.
8. No doc or help text introduced by this ticket claims zero-touch upgrade survival OR that a stale socket can never linger; wording matches the healing model (re-validate on owning foreground invocation, or repair) and the honest socket claim (stop never unlinks; start reclaims confirmed-stale under the held port; residual same-UID interference documented).
9. Headless documentation states the logged-in-session definition and the SSH-only foreground-run path with no reboot-persistence promise.

## Risks
launchd semantics vary across macOS versions and the declared support matrix is still undefined. The nvm-version-removal case leaves the recorded node path dangling — it must degrade to a detectable, recorded state, not a KeepAlive crash loop (interaction between launchd respawn and T-014's host-side breaker needs explicit reasoning). The start-path reclaim's residual same-UID window is accepted, not solved — user-facing text overclaiming here would void the honesty stance, and the adversarial competing-binder test is what keeps the claim honest. The matrix is the most infrastructure-expensive test surface in v0.3 (real reboots, real GUI MCP client launches); skimping on it silently voids the plan's round-2/round-3 honesty commitments.

## Open questions (owner decisions)
1. Test-infrastructure budget: does the owner want real Intel hardware/VMs for the reboot matrix, or is Apple Silicon-only acceptable for v0.3 with Intel deferred to the T-016 install matrix?
2. Which macOS versions must the matrix cover (same support-matrix decision flagged on T-014)?

**Related issues:** ISS-041, ISS-026
title: Menubar host + LaunchAgent: attach semantics, full upgrade matrix
